insurer: Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: ₹1,00,000 to ₹25,00,000 (as per tables in policy wording; exact SI depends on policy schedule)

great.name: Built-in Additional Sum Insured buffer (Recharge Benefit) after base cover is exhausted (can be used even for same illness / same hospitalization)
great.quote: Recharge Benefit (Applicable for A to K, M, S): If the limit of coverage under the policy is exhausted/ exceeded during the policy period, additional indemnity up to the limits stated in the table given below would be provided once for the remaining policy period. Such additional indemnity can be utilized even for the same hospitalization or for the treatment of diseases / illness / injury / for which claim was paid / payable under the policy.
great.explanation: This is an additional Sum Insured layer that activates after you fully use the Limit of Coverage, giving extra protection beyond the base cover.

great.name: NCB / Renewal Bonus that does NOT depend on claim-free years (Loyalty Bonus is irrespective of claim)
great.quote: Loyalty Bonus shall be available irrespective of a claim and only upon timely renewal without break or upon renewal within the grace period allowed.
great.explanation: Your cover can grow on renewal even if you have made claims, as long as you renew on time.

good.name: PED waiting period (Pre-existing diseases)
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a Pre-Existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with insurer
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are covered after 36 months (3 years) of continuous coverage, which is within normal market range.

good.name: Specific illness/procedure waiting period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the following listed Conditions, surgeries/ treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with us.
good.explanation: Specified conditions have a 24-month wait, which is standard.

good.name: Initial waiting period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.explanation: 30-day initial waiting is standard for non-accident illnesses.

good.name: Restore benefit (Automatic Restoration) - only for unrelated illness (not same illness)
good.quote: Automatic Restoration of Sum Insured... Such Automatic Restoration is available 3 times at 100% each time... It is made clear that such restored Sum Insured can be utilized only for illness / disease unrelated to the illness / diseases for which claim/s was / were made.
good.explanation: Restore is available but only for different/unrelated illnesses (not for the same illness).

good.name: Pre-hospitalization cover: 60 days
good.quote: Relevant Pre-Hospitalization medical expenses incurred for a period not exceeding 60 days prior to the date of hospitalization
good.explanation: Covers eligible medical expenses up to 60 days before admission (standard-good).

good.name: Post-hospitalization cover: 90 days
good.quote: Post Hospitalization medical expenses incurred for a period of 90 days from the date of discharge from the hospital
good.explanation: Covers eligible medical expenses for 90 days after discharge (standard-good).

good.name: Air ambulance cover (for SI ₹5 lakh and above)
good.quote: Air Ambulance charges up to 10% of the Sum Insured during the entire policy period... Note: This benefit is available for Sum Insured options of Rs.5,00,000/- and above only.
good.explanation: Air ambulance is covered (with limits and eligibility by SI), which is a meaningful add-on benefit.

good.name: Domiciliary hospitalization covered (with condition-wise exclusions)
good.quote: Domiciliary Hospitalization: Coverage for medical treatment (Including AYUSH) for a period exceeding three days...
good.explanation: Home-based treatment covered when hospitalization isn't feasible, but with a list of non-covered conditions.

good.name: Mandatory co-pay for seniors (20% for entry age 61+)
good.quote: This policy is subject to co- payment of 20% of each and every claim amount for fresh as well as renewal policies for insured persons whose age at the time of entry is 61 years and above.
good.explanation: 20% co-pay for senior entry age is common in many products; it reduces claim payout for that age band.

bad.name: Room rent has caps for lower sum insured (can trigger proportionate deductions)
bad.quote: Sum Insured (Rs.) Limit (Rs.) 1,00,000/- Upto 2,000/- per day ... 2,00,000/- 3,00,000/- Upto 5,000/- per day
bad.explanation: Daily room rent caps can lead to significant out-of-pocket expenses and proportionate deductions if you choose a higher room category.

bad.name: Proportionate deduction applies when room eligibility is exceeded (associated medical expenses)
bad.quote: Expenses relating to Associated medical expenses will be considered in proportion to the eligible room rent/room category stated in the policy schedule or actuals whichever is less.
bad.reference: Section 2 Coverage, Clause A Note + Definitions (Associated medical expenses) (pages 7/35 and 6/35)
bad.explanation: If you take a room above your eligibility, related doctor/OT/nursing charges may be reduced proportionately, increasing your share.

bad.name: Consumables not covered (explicitly excluded from 'Associated Medical Expenses' and also not stated as covered separately)
bad.quote: Associated Medical Expenses does not include cost of pharmacy and consumables, cost of implants and medical devices and cost of diagnostics, ICU charges...
bad.reference: Definitions, Specific Definitions: Associated Medical Expenses (page 6/35)
bad.explanation: Consumables (gloves, syringes, PPE kits etc.) are not stated as covered; this typically leads to out-of-pocket costs.

bad.name: Disease sub-limit: Cataract capped (varies by sum insured)
bad.quote: Expenses incurred on treatment of Cataract is subject to the limit as per the following table
bad.explanation: Cataract has a fixed cap per eye/policy period, which can be restrictive if hospital packages are higher.

bad.name: Modern treatments have sub-limits (not at actuals)
bad.quote: Coverage for Modern Treatments: The following expenses are payable... is limited to the amount mentioned in table below.
bad.explanation: Even though modern treatments are covered, the sub-limits can leave large gaps versus actual costs.

bad.name: Emergency road ambulance benefit is very low
bad.quote: Emergency Road ambulance charges up-to a sum of Rs. 750/- per hospitalization and overall limit of Rs.1,500/- per policy period
bad.explanation: Ambulance costs are often much higher; this limit can mean substantial out-of-pocket.

bad.name: No explicit NCB wording as 'No Claim Bonus' (policy uses Loyalty Bonus; if Loyalty Bonus not applicable for lower SI, SI may not grow)
bad.quote: For the Sum Insured options Rs.3,00,000/- and above, the insured would be entitled to benefit of Loyalty Bonus of 10%...
bad.explanation: If you choose a Sum Insured below ₹3 lakh, there is no stated renewal bonus/NCB growth benefit in this wording.

unclear.name: Co-pay for ages below 61 at entry (not explicitly stated as 0% or otherwise)
unclear.quote: Mandatory Co-payment... for insured persons whose age at the time of entry is 61 years and above.
unclear.explanation: The policy clearly states co-pay for entry age 61+, but does not explicitly confirm whether co-pay is 0% for others. Verify in the policy schedule/benefit table (and whether any other co-pay clauses apply).

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
